name: Marcus King Band
bio: Marcus King is a South Carolina guitarist and singer who has been working as a professional musician since he was a teenager, and his playing sits where blues, southern rock and soul overlap. His recent record Darling Blue is openly about coming through a hard stretch and out the other side, and that candor carries into how he performs live. This is his first time closing the Telluride Blues & Brews main stage.

name: Taj Mahal & Keb' Mo'
bio: Two elder statesmen of American blues — Henry St. Claire Fredericks Jr. and Kevin Roosevelt Moore — touring the pairing that won them a Grammy for Best Contemporary Blues Album with 2017's TajMo, now extended by the newer collection Room on the Porch. The set leans warm and conversational rather than loud: acoustic-forward blues, two voices trading lines, songs pitched as a place to put your guard down. Taj Mahal has deep history with this specific venue, having joined The Allman Brothers Band here in 1991 and again with Gregg Allman in 2015.

name: Jon Batiste
bio: A New Orleans–born pianist and bandleader who trained at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts and then Juilliard, where he took a master's in jazz. Wide audiences know him from more than 300 episodes fronting Stay Human as the house band on The Late Show. His awards shelf includes five Grammy wins from twenty nominations plus an Academy Award, Golden Globe, BAFTA and NAACP Image Award for his work on the film Soul. He closes the 2026 festival.

name: Daniel Donato's Cosmic Country
bio: Guitarist Daniel Donato calls his band's sound "Cosmic Country" and describes it as a frequency more than a genre — outlaw country and bluegrass pushed through psychedelic jam improvisation. He has framed the approach as deliberately living between order and chaos. The band plays twice at the 2026 festival: the Thursday-night opening show at the Sheridan Opera House and a late-afternoon Main Stage slot on Friday.

name: The Record Company
bio: An LA trio — Chris Vos, Alex Stiff and Marc Cazorla — playing gritty, riff-driven Delta-inflected blues rock. Their 2016 debut Give It Back to You was recorded in Stiff's living room on no budget and still earned a Grammy nomination; 2026 is a year-long anniversary tour behind that record. They previously played the festival in 2023.

name: Samantha Fish
bio: A Kansas City guitarist and singer who first played Telluride in 2017 and, per the festival, has returned every year since. Her records are emotionally direct blues rock and have drawn Grammy nominations; the most recent, 2025's Paper Doll, foregrounds her vocals alongside the guitar work. Her live sets are the high-energy end of the bill.

name: G. Love & Special Sauce
bio: Garrett Dutton, working as G. Love, has spent three decades splicing loose hip-hop phrasing onto blues harmonica and guitar — the self-titled 1994 debut, 2001's Electric Mile, and solo records including The Hustle, Lemonade, Fixin' to Die and The Juice. The delivery is relaxed and the lyrics are sharper than they first sound. He is a returning Telluride performer.

name: Charlie Musselwhite & GA-20
bio: Charlie Musselwhite is a Blues Hall of Fame harmonica player with a career spanning the classic Chicago era to a well-known collaboration with Ben Harper. GA-20 — named for a Gibson amplifier built from 1950 to 1961 — was started in 2018 by Boston guitarist Matthew Stubbs, who had been in Musselwhite's band, and plays a deliberately stripped-back, raw Chicago blues. This is the two acts reuniting as one billing.

name: Tab Benoit
bio: From Houma, Louisiana, Tab Benoit plays swamp blues on a well-worn Fender Telecaster Thinline, taught in his youth by Louisiana blues players living nearby. He has twice been named B.B. King Entertainer of the Year at the Blues Music Awards. He also co-authored a book on the blues and mental health, written partly to reduce stigma and partly to raise money for the HART Fund.

name: Eggy
bio: A Connecticut quartet — Jake Brownstein, Dani Battat, Mike Goodman and Alex Bailey — working the modern jam-band lane with actual songwriting underneath the improvisation. Their 2024 album Waiting Game was co-produced by James Petralli of White Denim, and the touring since has taken them to Austin City Limits, Electric Forest and Suwannee Hulaween.

name: Eddie 9V
bio: Brooks Mason, performing as Eddie 9V, has played since he was six and points at Rory Gallagher, Muddy Waters, Howlin’ Wolf and Freddie King as his reference points. His latest record is Saratoga. He last played Telluride in 2022 and returns to both a Main Stage slot and the Sunday closing show.

name: Greyhounds
bio: Guitarist Andrew Trube and keyboardist Anthony Farrell met in Austin in the late 1990s and have split songwriting and singing ever since, first pitching songs to artists including Derek Trucks and Susan Tedeschi. The catalogue is soul-leaning blues funk; the newest is Austin to Tulsa, made with King Cabbage Brass Band.

name: Judith Hill
bio: Judith Hill sang backing vocals for Prince, Michael Jackson and Stevie Wonder and appears in the documentary 20 Feet From Stardom. She now fronts her own band, writing blues-funk that pulls on gospel, soul and jazz, and she plays guitar — an instrument she has described choosing because it comes closest to the expressive range of the human voice.

name: Nether Hour
bio: An Austin trio — Bobby Flaco on vocals and guitar, Bishop on lead guitar and mandolin, Bercy on bass — mixing Louisiana swamp grooves with Texas funk, blues, soul and rock. They built their reputation on dive bars and roadhouse rooms and play loud.

name: Myron Elkins
bio: A Michigan songwriter and former welder whose 2023 debut Factories, Farms and Amphetamines was made in Nashville with producer Dave Cobb. He left Nashville for Memphis to record 2025's Nostalgia for Sale, keeping the heartland country-blues-rock frame but with a more weathered point of view.

name: DK Harrell
bio: From Ruston, Louisiana, D.K. Harrell pairs stinging single-note guitar lines with church-trained vocals. He has won a Blues Music Award and records for Alligator, where his debut Talkin’ Heavy landed him coverage in Living Blues, Vintage Guitar and Blues Music Magazine. He is one of the most visible young players in the current blues wave.

name: The Harlem Gospel Travelers
bio: Vocalists Ifedayo Gatling, Dennis Bailey and George Marage sing gospel with the arrangement sensibility of mid-1960s soul and funk. Their album Rhapsody follows 2021’s Look Up! and grew out of a suggestion from their mentor Eli "Paperboy" Reed to reinterpret gospel-funk material from the Numero Group reissue catalogue.

name: J & The Causeways
bio: A New Orleans R&B and soul band fronted by singer and keyboardist Jordan Anderson — the "J" — that formed at the Maple Leaf Bar. Horns, big vocals and a band that plays loose without falling apart. Anderson talks about the group as consciously representing the city’s musical lineage.

name: Kirk Fletcher
bio: An LA-born, Nashville-based guitarist, singer and producer with multiple Blues Music Award nominations and a run of Billboard Blues chart placements. He has been a go-to collaborator for Joe Bonamassa, Kim Wilson and The Fabulous Thunderbirds. His album Heartache By The Pound was recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals and leans on horns and gospel phrasing.

name: David Jacobs-Strain and Bob Beach
bio: A duo built around slide guitar and harmonica trading lines with each other. The material swings between wry, subversive blues, quiet ballads and swampy hard-driving rock, with a West Coast storytelling bent.

name: The Zac Schulze Gang
bio: A UK trio — guitarist and vocalist Zac Schulze with drummer Ben Schulze and bassist Ant Greenwell — playing loud, unfussy blues-rooted rock. Their debut Straight To It draws on Rory Gallagher and Dr. Feelgood, and they came up on the DIY circuit before breakouts at Rory Gallagher’s Tribute Festival and Eric Clapton’s Crossroads. They hold multiple UK Blues Awards including Young Artist of the Year.

name: Derrick Dove & The Peacekeepers
bio: An award-winning southern-fried blues rock band out of the South Georgia pines near Tifton, led by guitarist, vocalist and bandleader Derrick Dove. Gritty blues, soul grooves and classic-rock energy, played for a crowd. They have the most set assignments of any 2026 artist — four across three days.

name: Ken Valdez
bio: Originally from the high desert around Santa Fe and now based in Minneapolis, Ken Valdez is a guitarist with a rough-edged, soulful voice who folds blues, rock, funk and Latin music into one sound. He describes his own writing as melody-first.

name: Nigel Wearne & The Spectres
bio: The Australian winner of the 2025 Telluride Blues Challenge, returning the following year as part of the standing prize. His writing sits closer to Tom Waits, Nick Cave and Rickie Lee Jones than to twelve-bar orthodoxy — jazzy inflections, larger arrangements and homespun country blues in the same set.

name: Katie Skene
bio: A guitarist and songwriter who came up in the Tallahassee blues scene, spent a decade in the California jam circuit, and now works out of Nashville. She calls the result Cosmic Swamp Americana: electric southern blues and jam-band exploration over a heavy groove, with keys and slide-leaning guitar. Allman Brothers and Grateful Dead are the obvious lineage.

name: Alex Maryol
bio: A Santa Fe–based blues-rock player with rough vocals and expressive guitar, mixing Delta blues, indie rock, R&B and Chicago blues. Once written up as a blues prodigy, he has since shared stages with Etta James, Bonnie Raitt, Lyle Lovett, Leon Russell and Blues Traveler, and has played King Biscuit as well as this festival.

name: Little Willie Farmer
bio: A lifelong resident of Duck Hill, Mississippi who spent decades working as an auto mechanic and playing nights and weekends, drawing on Muddy Waters, Howlin’ Wolf and Lightnin’ Hopkins. He is a Music Maker Relief Foundation partner artist. His 2019 album The Man From the Hill earned the critical attention that let him leave the repair shop for music full time.

name: Albert White
bio: An Atlanta native who learned playing behind his uncle Piano Red — the R&B hitmaker whose "Doctor Feelgood" the Beatles later covered. White and his band The Rockers have worked jukes, clubs and celebrations across the Southeast since the 1960s, sharing bills with Rufus Thomas, Ray Charles, The Tams and Joe Tex. His set carries the high-energy funky R&B side of that tradition.

name: Terry "Harmonica" Bean
bio: A Mississippi player who was headed for baseball until a motorcycle accident redirected him to harmonica and guitar. He plays hill country blues and is precise about the difference from Delta style — where Delta players sat still and worked in open tunings with slides and picks, hill country players used the whole porch, stomping and moving, in unusual tunings.

name: Scramble Campbell
bio: Keith "Scramble" Campbell paints the festival as it happens, working from a small riser beside the sound tower and finishing a canvas by the time the set ends. The approach is borrowed from Leroy Neiman, who did the same at sporting events; Campbell applied it to music instead. He has been a fixture at Blues & Brews for many years.

name: Troy Walker
bio: A comedian and writer whose credits include VICE’s Flophouse and writing for both the 95th and 96th Academy Awards ceremonies. He recently recorded a debut album. Some press coverage of the lineup announcement billed the comedy segment as "Troy Walker & Friends."

name: Baron Vaughn
bio: A comedian, actor and director best known as Bud on Netflix’s Grace and Frankie opposite Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, and as the voice of Tom Servo in recent Mystery Science Theater 3000 seasons. He co-created and co-hosted The New Negroes with Open Mike Eagle, co-created Call & Response, and made the documentary project Fatherless.

name: Kiran Deol
bio: A comedian and actor who starred in Didn’t Die at Sundance 2025, where Paste called it a star-making turn. Her screen work includes Sunnyside (NBC/Hulu), Destroy All Neighbors, How to Get Away with Murder, Modern Family and Freakier Friday.

name: Hannah Jones
bio: A Denver-based comedian who was homeschooled in a conservative religious co-op and now builds material out of sex, dating and gender politics. Her short-form video has been viewed tens of millions of times. She has appeared on Netflix Is A Joke Radio and Don’t Tell Secret Sets, been written up in Denverite and Westword, and opened for Josh Gondelman, Atsuko Okatsuka and Kumail Nanjiani. She is a regular at Denver’s Comedy Works.

name: Brewers Showcase
bio: The festival’s beer tasting programme, presented by the Telluride Blues Society and held in the Beer Garden between the Main Stage and the Blues Stage. Three of the four sessions pour 70+ styles from 25+ breweries plus a Colorado Brewers Guild tent; the late Saturday session is the rare list — 35 or more high-ABV, barrel-aged, wild and non-traditional beers. 21+, and a Single-Day or 3-Day festival pass is required in addition to the tasting ticket.

name: Blisters & Brews 5K
bio: The Saturday-morning 5K in Elks Park, $35 to enter, benefiting the Telluride Adaptive Sports Program.

name: Yoga Sessions
bio: Free guided yoga in Elks Park on Saturday and Sunday morning, 10:00–11:00 AM. Open to everyone; no ticket required.

name: Blues For Breakfast
bio: The Saturday and Sunday morning session at the Elks Lodge, 9:00 AM–12:00 PM. On Saturday it runs alongside the Telluride Blues Challenge, whose winner takes a 15-minute Main Stage slot the same afternoon and returns to play the following year’s festival.

name: 2026 Telluride Blues Challenge Winner
bio: A 15-minute Main Stage slot on Saturday afternoon awarded to the winner of that morning’s Telluride Blues Challenge at the Elks Lodge. The performer is decided on the day, so the official schedule lists the slot without a name. The 2025 winner was Nigel Wearne, who returns to the 2026 bill as part of the standing prize.
